title: Artificial Urgency & Time Limit
explanation: Scammers create false panic with tight deadlines so you act before thinking.

title: Threat of Disconnection or Legal Action
explanation: Threatening sudden disconnection or police arrest is a classic fear tactic used by fraudsters.

title: Request to Share OTP / Secret Code
patterns: (share|send|provide|give|reply with)\s*(your)?\s*(secret|banking|login)?\s*(otp|one time password|pin)\s*(with our|to our|to cancel|to prevent|to verify|to unblock|immediately|over call)
explanation: Legitimate banks and services will never ask you to disclose or reply with your OTP.

title: Fake Security / Unauthorized Debit Alert
explanation: Scammers fabricate unauthorized transactions to panic you into sharing security codes.

title: Card Details / PIN / CVV Request
patterns: (enter|share|submit|update)\s*(your)?\s*(cvv|atm pin|card expiry|credit card number|debit card pin)
explanation: Asking for your CVV, ATM PIN, or card details is a direct attempt to steal your funds.

title: Pay-to-Receive / UPI Collect Trick
patterns: (enter|enter your)\s*(upi pin|pin)\s*(to receive|to accept|to credit|to claim)
(scan|scan this)\s*(qr|qr code)\s*(to receive|to get money|for refund|to credit)
money will be credited after entering pin
explanation: Entering a UPI PIN or scanning a QR code always sends money from your account, it never receives money.

title: Unsolicited UPI Refund or Cashback Request
explanation: Scammers disguise debit collect requests as cashbacks or refunds to trick you into entering your PIN.

title: Fake KYC Expiry / Account Suspension
explanation: Banks do not send unverified links to update KYC; they ask you to visit an official branch or app.

title: Bank Account Suspension Claim
explanation: Fraudulent messages falsely claim your bank account is blocked to lure you into phishing sites.

title: Job Offer Requiring Upfront Fee
explanation: Legitimate employers never demand registration fees, security deposits, or advance training charges.

title: Unrealistic Part-Time Pay Offer
patterns: earn rs [0-9]+ per day working from home
explanation: Promises of high daily income for minimal online tasks are typical lures for task or deposit scams.

title: Unofficial Messaging Contact for Employment
explanation: Legitimate companies recruit through official corporate emails and portals, not anonymous chat handles.

title: Lottery or Lucky Draw Winner Claim
explanation: You cannot win a lottery or contest you never entered; these messages aim for advance fee fraud.

title: Upfront Processing Fee or Deposit Request
explanation: Demanding advance fees or tax deposits before releasing a prize or loan is always a scam.

title: Pre-Approved Loan With No Verification
explanation: Predatory loan apps advertise loans without CIBIL or documentation to harvest personal data.

title: Aggressive Loan Recovery Threat
patterns: legal action will be taken.*loan not paid.*send notice
explanation: Illegal lending apps employ harassment, extortion, and contact-list shaming tactics.

title: Shortened URL in Text Message
explanation: Shortened links hide the real destination domain and are frequently used to conceal scam websites.

title: Direct IP Address Link
explanation: Legitimate businesses use domain names, not raw numerical IP addresses.

title: Suspicious or Low-Cost Web Extension
explanation: Domains ending in .xyz, .top, or .click are disproportionately favored by disposable scam sites.

title: Fake Parcel Delivery Failure
patterns: (update|confirm) your address.*(to receive parcel|within 24 hours|within 12 hours)
explanation: Scammers send fake courier alerts asking for nominal re-delivery fees to capture credit card numbers.

title: Traffic Challan / Fine Impersonation
explanation: Scam messages imitate traffic police challans and prompt users to install malicious APKs.

title: Fake Income Tax / Government Subsidy
patterns: tax refund credited to account.*confirm account details
explanation: Impersonating the tax department to offer sudden refunds is an attempt to steal banking credentials.

title: Remote Access Tool Request
patterns: support executive will guide via anydesk
explanation: Fraudsters ask victims to install screen-sharing software to take total control of their device and bank apps.

title: External Android APK Download
explanation: Direct links to APK files bypass the official Play Store and often contain banking trojans or spyware.

title: Direct Mobile Callback for Urgent Issue
patterns: (call immediately|contact officer|call helpline|call manager|contact our power officer)\s*(at|on)?\s*(\+91[ -]?)?[6-9][0-9]{9}
explanation: Official banks and utilities use registered toll-free or short-code numbers, not personal mobile phone numbers.

title: Unsolicited Password / PIN Reset
patterns: reset your netbanking password here: https?:
explanation: Phishing messages claim unauthorized password changes to trick you into clicking malicious verification links.

title: High-Frequency Scam Terminology
explanation: Contains phrasing commonly associated with mass phishing and online financial fraud campaigns.

title: Bank Name Coupled with Suspicious Domain
explanation: Mimicking trusted bank or payment brands on unofficial domain names is a strong sign of phishing.
